_sources.discrepancies: NCSL classifies RI as 'photo ID requested' (not required). Rhode Island requests but does not require photo ID; voters without an acceptable photo ID may cast a regular ballot after providing their name, address, and signature. Rhode Island enacted no-excuse absentee voting in 2021. Registration deadline is 30 days before the election per RI law. 2026-06-10 verification: the 2024-carry-forward primary date of Sept 8 was WRONG — the RI Board of Elections lists the 2026 Statewide Primary as WEDNESDAY, September 9, 2026 (registration deadline 8/10/26; mail ballot application deadline 8/19/26; early voting begins 8/20/26). General 11/3/26: registration deadline 10/4/26; mail ballot application 10/13/26; early voting 10/14/26 through the day before. Early-voting windows corrected from 2024 carry-forwards.

earlyVoting.notes: In-person early voting at your local board of canvassers begins August 20, 2026 and runs through 4 p.m. the day before the primary. The 2026 statewide primary is on a Wednesday (September 9).
In-person early voting at local boards of canvassers begins October 14, 2026 and runs through 4 p.m. the day before Election Day.
Rhode Island offers in-person early voting at local boards of canvassers from 20 days before the election through 4 p.m. the day before. No-excuse absentee mail voting is also available.

votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: Rhode Island does not have a statewide prohibition on phones in polling places. Voters may not photograph their ballot or other voters. Electioneering is prohibited within 50 feet of a polling place entrance.
additionalRules: Photo ID is requested but not required. Voters without an acceptable photo ID may sign the poll book and vote a regular ballot after providing their name and address.
Semi-closed primary: registered party members vote in their party's primary. Unaffiliated voters may not vote in partisan primaries.
No-excuse absentee voting is available for all registered voters.

eligibility: Any registered voter may request a mail ballot without providing a reason (no-excuse absentee voting, enacted 2021)
voteByMail.applicationDeadline: 4 days before the election (received by local board of canvassers); online/in-person applications accepted until 4 days before
voteByMail.returnDeadline: Must be received by the local board of canvassers by 8 p.m. on Election Day
voteByMail.returnDeadlinePlain: Must arrive at the board of canvassers by 8 p.m. on Election Day. Postmarks do not count.

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: Rhode Island has a semi-closed primary (R.I. Gen. Laws §17-15-24). Registered party members vote in their party's primary. Unaffiliated voters may also request a party ballot and vote in a primary. After voting, they may return to unaffiliated status.
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: Rhode Island tiene una primaria semi-cerrada (R.I. Gen. Laws §17-15-24). Los miembros registrados en un partido votan en la primaria de su partido. Los votantes sin afiliación también pueden solicitar una boleta de partido y votar en una primaria. Después de votar, pueden volver al estatus sin afiliación.
